title: The Eighty-Dollar Champion: Snowman, the Horse That Inspired a Nation
author: Elizabeth Letts
target_audience: General readers interested in heartwarming true stories
Fans of sports and underdog tales
Readers seeking historical accounts of 1950s and 1960s America
Young adults and adults looking for motivational nonfiction
core_themes: The underdog triumphing against all odds
The American Dream in the postwar era
primary_purpose: To chronicle the extraordinary true story of Snowman, a plow horse rescued from slaughter, and his unlikely rise to show-jumping stardom with his owner Harry de Leyer during the 1950s, inspiring a nation with their journey of hope and resilience.

structure_format.narrative_style: Engaging, narrative nonfiction with historical detail and emotional depth
structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic chapters following the chronological journey of Snowman and Harry de Leyer, interwoven with context on American life and equestrian sport

key_concepts_lessons: Extraordinary potential may be found in the most unlikely places.
Resilience and kindness can transform lives—both human and animal.
Success comes not just from talent, but from belief, hard work, and compassion.
Societal context—such as postwar optimism—shapes the meaning and impact of individual triumphs.
Partnership between humans and animals can lead to remarkable achievements.
An underdog’s victory can inspire and unite a broad audience.
notable_features: True underdog story based on real events
Blends biography, sports history, and social commentary
Accessible for both equestrian insiders and general readers
Includes insights into the horse show world and mid-20th century American society
Recognized for its compelling, cinematic narrative
cultural_historical_context: Set during the optimistic years of post-World War II America, the story reflects themes of social mobility, the American Dream, and newfound hope. Snowman and Harry's journey captured the national imagination in a time when people looked for inspiring, unifying stories. The book also illuminates the changing landscape of American horse sports and the broader culture of the 1950s and 1960s.
reception_impact: Became a New York Times bestseller
Widely praised for its moving, well-researched narrative and accessibility to non-horse enthusiasts
Inspired a resurgence of interest in Snowman's legacy and equestrian sports
Often recommended in book clubs and educational settings as a feel-good, motivational read
Helped cement Snowman’s status as a cultural icon of perseverance and hope
